newsitem.title: INDIA: Hopes of lower Indian interest spurs gilt trading.
newsitem.headline: Hopes of lower Indian interest spurs gilt trading.

text.p: Expectations of falling interest rates following the announcement of the monetary policy on October 19 have led to a sharp increase in debt market activity, money market dealers and analysts said on Wednesday.

The Reserve Bank of India announces the monetary policy for the second half of financial 1996/97 (April-March) on Saturday amid widespread expectations that it will cut banks' cash reserve requirements in a bid to improve liquidity and reduce interest rates.

"A drop in interest rates will lead to an a rise in the prices of debt instruments," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Market players are picking up government securities at low prices now to sell at higher rates later."

Data from the National Stock Exchange show that the daily average trade in government securities on the exchange's wholesale debt market segment for the first two weeks of October has almost tripled to 2.3 billion rupees against a daily average of around 837 million rupees in September.

Several market players have taken long positions in government securities and treasury bills ahead of Saturday's policy announcement, ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said in its daily debt market report on Wednesday.
I-Sec said the players were taking positions hoping to book profits subsequent to favourable announcements in the policy.
